title: Onboarding minimal evidence pathway — UX draft
summary: Working draft exploring a lightweight onboarding flow for customer-managed networks that produces a minimal, queryable evidence bundle for future audits and approval gates. Focus: reduce friction for operators while preserving forensic fidelity and compliance needs.
goals: Design an onboarding UX that collects only the minimal required evidence for attestation and later forensic reconstruction
Enable fast self-serve onboarding for customers deploying Private (VPC / on-prem) while meeting enterprise audit needs
Define the shape and retention semantics of the 'onboard-evidence' bundle used by approval gates and support playbooks
Propose an operator-facing rollback/fallback surface powered by sampled audit traces
scope: Customer-managed VPCs and on-prem gateways for Private deployments
Evidence bundle definition (what fields, formats, hashes, timestamps)
Minimal UI flow in Console and CLI for operator consent and artifact submission
Integration points with approval gate (sync/async) and internal forensic index
non_goals: Full SIEM ingestion architecture (we'll hand off via standard exporters)
Replacing customer's own audit tooling — we aim to supplement with compact evidence
Designing long-term cold-storage forensic archives (this doc focuses on onboarding/short-term retention)
End-to-end cryptographic notary service (prototype attestation tokens only)
user_stories: As a network operator, I want to complete Private onboarding in < 20 minutes with clear guidance so I can get my model endpoints serving
As an SRE on the customer side, I want the Console to produce a tamper-evident bundle I can hand to my internal auditors
As a Redwood support engineer, I want a compact evidence summary so I can triage a failed approval gate quickly without pulling full logs
As a security reviewer, I want persistent hashes and provenance links so I can verify that evidence wasn't modified post-onboarding
requirements: R1: The onboarding flow must produce an 'onboard-evidence' JSONL bundle with named records (connection-probe, config-manifest, attestation-token, sampling-hash, agent-checkin)
R2: Each record must include a stable ISO-8601 timestamp, source id (customer-connector-id), and a SHA256 digest field
R3: Console UX shall offer 'express' vs 'verified' onboarding paths; express collects fewer records but triggers a higher-frequency sampling policy post-onboard
R4: Approval gates must be able to request a re-run evidence probe (async) if sampling reveals anomalies
R5: Retention defaults: 30 days full bundle retention, 365 days hashed index; configurable by enterprise contract
R6: The CLI installer emits a human-readable checklist and an opt-in telemetry statement (customer must consent to bundle upload)
R7: Evidence bundle size target: median < 250KB for common topologies (single-region VPC + gateway)
R8: Forensic playground: provide an internal tool to replay evidence bundles into the SRE triage UI
design_notes: Minimalism tradeoff: smaller bundle => faster onboarding but more reliance on sampled telemetry later
Agent checkin frequency during onboarding: 10s heartbeats for first 5 minutes, then backoff to 1m if express path chosen
Attestation-token is small (base64 signed blob) containing connector id, nonce, timestamp, and a key id referencing KMS signature
We should avoid shipping raw IP tables or full routing tables — instead capture hashes and summarized predicates (e.g., 'egress-restricted: true')
Provide 'evidence diff' UI card comparing current bundle to most recent approved bundle for rollback reasoning
Make evidence bundle schema versioned (schema_v, created_at) so consumers can evolve without breaking parsing
privacy_and_consent: Onboard flow must display a single-pane consent dialog explaining exactly which artifacts will be uploaded
Customers can choose 'local-only' mode where evidence is produced but not uploaded; Redwood support will require signed upload for troubleshooting
PII avoidance: explicit scanning to strip usernames, email addresses, and internal hostnames from freeform fields in manifests
We will publish a minimal privacy spec explaining retention, access, and redaction rules
approval_gate_integration: Pre-approval: fast-sanity checks (bundle presence, schema validity, attestation token signature)
Gate scoring: run a lightweight policy that outputs PASS/FLAG/HOLD based on e.g. routing predicates and evidence freshness
Escalation: FLAG bubbles to an operator queue with a compact evidence card and a one-click 'request additional probe' action
Automated fallback: if HOLD persists for > 15 minutes, model-serving routes to a hosted-compatible fallback (customer-configurable)
Audit trail: every approval decision must be persisted with user id, decision timestamp, and link to the onboard-evidence bundle
telemetry_and_metrics: Approval gate latency (median, p95) and pass/fail rates
Fraction of onboardings using 'express' path vs 'verified' path
Frequency of re-run probes per onboarding (indicator of instability)
Support cases opened citing insufficient evidence (triage metric)
operational_playbooks: Playbook A: Support triage for a failed approval (steps: pull bundle, validate signature, run replay tool, request additional probe)
Playbook B: Customer rollback flow (create evidence diff, apply previous approved bundle, coordinate with customer gateway admin)
Playbook C: Forensics sample retention and export (how to export hashed index to legal team on request)
open_questions: Q1: What is the minimal set of fields auditors will accept as 'forensic enough'? Need to sync with legal/compliance.
Q2: Should the onboard-evidence bundle be pushed to customer's own S3/KMS by default to avoid sending raw artifacts through Redwood?
Q3: How do we present hashed vs raw evidence in Console so customers understand when we can/ cannot help with troubleshooting?
Q4: What SLA do we commit to for re-run probe responses? Immediate (sync) probes add latency to onboarding.
Q5: Should express path create a 'probation' label in tenant metadata to surface in billing/alerts?
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Experiment — CLI prototype that emits a local evidence bundle and optional manual upload (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Console UX + schema v1 + attestation-token integration (4 weeks)
Phase 2: Approval gate policy engine hooks + replay tool for support (6 weeks)
Phase 3: Sampling/retention policies + contract-configurable defaults + docs (4 weeks)
Phase 4: Hardening, redaction automation, and compliance review (ongoing)
risks_mitigation: Risk: Customers distrust uploading any local artifacts. Mitigation: local-only mode and customer-pushed upload option
Risk: Evidence bundle grows too large. Mitigation: strict schema, strip raw logs, use hashes and summaries
Risk: Approval gating delays critical rollouts. Mitigation: express path with probation + automated fallback routing
Risk: Legal/regulatory rejection of minimal evidence. Mitigation: early sync with compliance and pilot customers
notes: Next steps: 1) Book 30m sync with Compliance (Elise) to validate required evidence fields 2) Build CLI prototype PR and share in #private-deployments 3) Recruit two pilot customers for express/verified flows — ask Solutions Eng to propose candidates
